cases.title: Vague landing page with no brand
cases.prompt: Make a landing page for a small-batch coffee roaster. It should feel premium but not like a generic SaaS page. I do not have a brand guide or an existing site.
cases.expected_output: A design brief that names the surface mode, a visual world with an avoid list, one focal motion moment, constraints, and out-of-scope work; then implementation guidance that uses motion tiers, reduced motion, and a verification report.

assertions.text: Names a surface mode from the skill's four modes
Names a visual world and an avoid or anti-reference list
Chooses one focal motion moment
Plans reduced-motion behavior, not just animation
Names the T0 reduced behavior
Names the T1 essential behavior
Reports verification with PASS and FAIL or BLOCKED results

cases.title: Operate dashboard redesign
cases.prompt: Redesign the metrics dashboard for my B2B SaaS. Operators stare at it all day; it should feel fast and clear, not decorative.
cases.expected_output: An Operate treatment: scanability and density over expression, a restrained motion role, keyboard and focus behavior, T0/T1 behavior, and a verification table.

assertions.text: Classifies the surface as Operate
Prioritizes density or scanability
Plans keyboard and focus behavior
Plans reduced-motion behavior
Names the T0 reduced behavior
Reports verification with PASS and FAIL or BLOCKED results

cases.title: Critique an intentionally flawed pricing page
cases.prompt: Critique the pricing page in `evals/fixtures/flawed-pricing/index.html`. I need to know what blocks shipping. If you cannot render it, say so.
cases.expected_output: A critique with located findings by severity, covering the page shipping no script so every control is inert, the infinite animation and missing reduced-motion handling, low contrast, the unnamed icon button, removed focus styles, the image without dimensions, the two competing superlative badges, and the message the page never states: what it is, who it is for, what the action does, and what the price costs per period; a verdict from the critique vocabulary.

assertions.text: Finds that the page ships no script, so its controls are inert
Finds the two competing superlative badges
Finds the infinite animation or pulse
Connects the animation to reduced-motion handling
Finds a contrast problem
Uses a numeric contrast criterion
Finds the icon button without an accessible name
Finds the removed focus indicator
Finds the image without width/height attributes or CLS risk
Assigns findings a severity
Ends with a critique verdict
Reports that the hero or fold communicates no offer, audience, or action, and names the change
Reports that the prices carry no period or unit

cases.title: Parallax and 3D on a low-end phone
cases.prompt: Build a product page with a parallax hero and 3D cards, but it must work on a low-end Android phone and with reduced motion enabled.
cases.expected_output: A T0/T1-first build: parallax becomes static, 3D degrades or lazy-loads, the tier attribute is present, a performance budget is stated, and verification is reported.

assertions.text: Gives parallax a static or disabled T0 fallback
Gives the 3D or tilt effect a fallback, lazy load, tier cap, or gate
Uses the data-motion-tier attribute
States a performance budget
Plans reduced-motion behavior
Names the T0 reduced behavior
Reports verification with PASS and FAIL or BLOCKED results

cases.title: Photoreal real piece on the web, then other platforms
cases.prompt: We sell a machined aluminium espresso tamper. Build the product page section that renders the actual piece with Three.js: it has to look like the real thing, be true to size and colour, work on a low-end phone, and we may reuse the same model in our Unity app and a Flutter app later.
cases.expected_output: A three.js render plan for a real piece: metre scale, a camera matched to product photography, a PBR environment and a contact shadow, colour management that preserves the brand colour, a compressed and validated glTF, tiered fallbacks, and a per-platform route for the same model.

assertions.text: Works in metres or millimetres instead of arbitrary units
Matches the camera to product photography or names a lens/FOV decision
Uses an environment map, HDRI, or PMREM for PBR realism
Grounds the piece with a contact or grounding shadow
Names tone mapping, colour space, or an exposure decision
Specifies material response with metalness, roughness, clearcoat, or transmission
Compresses and validates the glTF instead of shipping the raw export
Keeps a poster, turntable, or photo-set fallback below the realtime tier
Plans reduced-motion behavior
Routes the same model to another platform's own library
Reports verification with PASS and FAIL or BLOCKED results

cases.title: Scroll that feels like flying forward, then native apps
cases.prompt: Our travel startup wants the homepage hero to feel like you are flying forward through three destinations as you scroll down: mountains, then a city, then a beach. It has to stay smooth on a cheap Android phone, respect people who get motion sick, and we tell the same story in our Flutter app and our SwiftUI iPad app.
cases.expected_output: A pinned scroll-depth stage where one progress value moves layers forward along Z under perspective, three stops paced inside a scroll-length budget, depth cues without animated blur, a static stack for reduced motion, tiered simplification for low-end devices, readable content order, and the Flutter and SwiftUI equivalents.

assertions.text: Moves content or a camera forward along the Z axis instead of only offsetting planes vertically
Pins the scene while the page scrolls
Drives the choreography from one scroll progress value or timeline
Uses perspective as the main depth cue
Treats animated blur as expensive or avoids it
Honours the reduced-motion preference
Falls back to a static, readable layout
Simplifies per device capability or motion tier
Bounds the pinned scroll length or paces the stops
Keeps the stops readable in source order for assistive technology
Names a real Flutter API for the same effect
Names a real SwiftUI API for the same effect
